name: Luana Soares
title: Postdoctoral Researcher · Uppsala University
tagline: I'm passionate about understanding the complexity of life, especially how species become species: through hybridization, rapid divergence and polyploidy.
bio: I am a postdoctoral researcher and Birgitta Sintring Fellow in Plant Ecology and Evolution at the Department of Ecology and Genetics, Uppsala University, Sweden, where I work with Mario Vallejo-Marín. My research now centres on polyploidy: using Mimulus peregrinus, a monkeyflower that arose less than 150 years ago through hybridization and whole-genome duplication, I study how new polyploid species form, and what happens to their genomes, in near real time.

What drives me is the question of how species become species. To answer it I move between scales, from population genomics to species-level phylogenomics, and many of my questions are answered with species-level data alone. I have worked on hybridization, introgression, rapid radiations and species delimitation, mostly in Solanaceae (Petunia and Nicotiana) from the subtropical highland grasslands of southern South America.

As a side quest, I also hold a postdoc at the Department of Botany of the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), Brazil, with Caroline Turchetto, on the evolutionary history and conservation of Nicotiana sect. Alatae. Before Uppsala, I was a postdoctoral researcher at IBMCP (CSIC-UPV) in Valencia, Spain, and I did my PhD and MSc in Genetics and Molecular Biology at UFRGS with Loreta B. Freitas.
On this site you'll find my publications, the tutorials and reproducible pipelines I use in my work, and my up-to-date CV.

current_projects.title: How new polyploid species form: population genomic insights from Mimulus peregrinus
current_projects.funder: Uppsala University · Birgitta Sintring Fellowship · with Mario Vallejo-Marín · from November 2026
current_projects.summary: Mimulus peregrinus is one of the youngest known polyploid plant species. It arose in Scotland from hybridization between two introduced monkeyflowers, M. guttatus and M. luteus, followed by whole-genome duplication, and it formed independently at least twice. Using whole-genome resequencing, I will characterize how the parental subgenomes are retained, exchanged or lost after polyploidization, and test whether natural selection shapes these early genome changes.
current_projects.label: Main project

current_projects.title: Evolutionary history, genetic diversity and conservation of Nicotiana sect. Alatae in the Campos Sulinos
current_projects.funder: UFRGS, Department of Botany, Brazil · CAPES AURORA Program · with Caroline Turchetto
current_projects.summary: Using DArT-seq genomic data, I study the diversity, population structure, lineage delimitation, gene flow and hybridization of Nicotiana species from the southern Brazilian grasslands. I combine genomic, environmental and spatial data to map genetic diversity, model habitat suitability, find historical and future climate refugia, and identify priority areas for conservation. I also build reproducible pipelines and train students in bioinformatics and genomic data analysis.
